source_title: ‘Ghosts’ Star Asher Grodman Teases What’s Next for Pete After Halloween Twist (Exclusive) - People.com
source_excerpt:
Asher Grodman teases what’s ahead for Pete, Trevor and the rest of the ghosts when the series returns for its Christmas special in December
Sabienna Bowman is a Staff Editor at PEOPLE, working on the News Team. She joined the brand in 2023. She previously worked at POPSUGAR, Bustle and Scarymommy.
Warning: This article contains spoilers for Ghosts ’ season 6 Halloween special, now streaming on Paramount+.
Ghosts ’ season 6 Halloween special aired Thursday, Oct. 30, on CBS
Star Asher Grodman tells PEOPLE his reaction to the twist ending and teases what’s next for the characters
The actor says the twist opens up “exciting” possibilities for the future of the show
Pete is back — but in true Ghosts fashion, there’s a twist.
The season 6 Halloween special, which aired Thursday, Oct. 30, on CBS, picked up a few months after the end of season 5 with Sam ( Rose McIver ) in Australia filming her Christmas movie and Pete (Richie Moriarty) still missing after he disappeared in the finale.
“The Mirror – Parts One & Two” kicks off the new season by establishing the ghosts and Jay’s ( Utkarsh Ambudkar ) dynamic with temporary ghost-minder Kyle (Ben Feldman), hosting an unexpected family reunion for Hetty (Rebecca Wisocky) and bringing Pete back into the fold sans memory.
That last twist surprised Asher Grodman, who plays pantsless ghost Trevor, but the actor tells PEOPLE it also opens up “exciting” possibilities moving forward.
“We have the thing with Pete and his memory, which is a fun idea because at the core of the show, I always feel like the relationship of the eight ghosts is really the central motor of what makes this show unique,” Grodman, 39, says. “How many shows do you have relationships that have lasted for hundreds of years? So they’ve all in essence lost a big part of their life because even though Pete’s there, he’s not really there.”
Grodman adds that “the prospect of playing with that” is “exciting” as he looks ahead to the rest of the season.
The episode ends with Pete reappearing on the Woodstone property on his death day. His reappearance comes after he stayed away too long last season and vanished on the way home from England with Jay and Kyle. However, it’s quickly apparent that Pete has no memory of his last 40 years as a ghost.
Grodman reveals Pete will still be dealing with his ghostly amnesia when the show returns in December for an hour-long Christmas special.
“He’s right where we left him at Christmas,” the actor shares, adding that the holiday special will feature an homage to Die Hard .
“We have this Christmas episode coming up that has this Die Hard theme, and Trevor will be very involved in the mayhem and the resolution of that episode as well,” Grodman says. “So he’s got his fingerprints on a lot of the trouble and the resolution of that. That’s a fun one. You get to see a few of these characters in ways you’ve never seen them before. ... It’s a very high-stakes episode, I will say.”
Season 6 also brings a major landmark for the Ghosts cast as the series is set to hit its 100th episode in 2027. The significance of being on a show that’s still going strong after six seasons isn’t lost on Grodman.
“It is a very rare thing and we’re lucky to be able to make something and have a job and have this show resonate with people. Even that is just a wild thing. When you set off to be an actor, you dream of stuff like this, but the odds of it happening are pretty slim,” he says.
Grodman continues, “It’s just a collaborative, joyful process. The fact that we’ve done 100 of these episodes and we’re all still sitting here like, ‘God, I hope we get to do a few more years of this,’ because it’s just fun to go to work.”
Ghosts season 6 continues in December with a one-hour Christmas special on CBS. Seasons 1 through 5, as well as the Halloween special, are available to stream now on Paramount+.
